fullPassage: What would a language be like if it didn’t make any simplifications or generalizations? (A) There might be some superintelligent race of beings that could know such a language, but they would have to know virtually everything in the world to learn all these names. Human language has taken a different route — many fewer names, with a loss of precision, but a basic vocabulary that is readily acquired. However, this fact is not simply a compromise with our limited cognitive capacity. (B) By using the same word for different objects, we’re communicating information about those things. Calling two different-looking things “spider” communicates that they probably have eight legs, weave nests, eat insects, and other noticeable details, which we would not know if we gave them all their own separate names. (C) It would be a language in which every word was a proper noun. Because you don’t want to gloss over the differences between snakes that are slightly different in some respect, every snake must have its own name. Furthermore, every event must have its own verb, because not every occasion of thinking or dancing or talking is identical.

questions.passage: What would a language be like if it didn’t make any simplifications or generalizations? There might be some superintelligent race of beings that could know such a language, but they would have to know virtually everything in the world to learn all these names. <u>Human language has taken a different route</u> — many fewer names, with a loss of precision, but a basic vocabulary that is readily acquired. However, this fact is not simply a compromise with our limited cognitive capacity. By using the same word for different objects, we’re communicating information about those things. Calling two different-looking things “spider” communicates that they probably have eight legs, weave nests, eat insects, and other noticeable details, which we would not know if we gave them all their own separate names. It would be a language in which every word was a proper noun. Because you don’t want to gloss over the differences between snakes that are slightly different in some respect, every snake must have its own name. Furthermore, every event must have its own verb, because not every occasion of thinking or dancing or talking is identical.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 Human language has taken a different route가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ‘다른 길을 택했다’ = 모든 것에 고유명사 부여 대신 단순화/일반화를 선택.
det.analysis:
① 동물과 다른 방식 — 동물 비교가 아닌 가상 언어와의 대비
② 개별 명명 대신 범주화로 단순화 — 고유명사 언어와 대비하여 fewer names 선택 ←정답
③ 새 문법 체계 발명 — 문법이 아닌 어휘 수 축소
④ 정밀성 포기, 다양성 추구 — 다양성이 아닌 단순화가 핵심
det.tip: different route = 고유명사 언어(가상) vs. 인간 언어(단순화)
